For Sonnet 4.6 same-model, precondition completeness increases by 3 tasks at k = 3 k=3 and 6 tasks at k = 10 k=10 . Those changes do not translate into strict pass@1 because postconditions deteriorate: postcondition soundness falls by 13 tasks at k = 3 k=3 and 19 tasks at k = 10 k=10 , while postcondition completeness falls by 7 and 15 tasks. Claude Sonnet 5 shows a related postcondition-sensitive pattern at k = 10 k=10 , losing 6 tasks on postcondition soundness and 11 tasks on postcondition completeness. Sonnet 4.6 to GPT-5.6 and Sonnet 4.6 to Gemini 3.8 Flash avoid large postcondition losses. Overall, the failure analysis shows that final Lean results depend on whether the complete pipeline expresses the reference-grounded clarification in compilable and semantically correct specifications. Postconditions have the largest observed degradations; failures there can erase positive changes elsewhere. The qualitative cases reveal two distinct strict-score mechanisms: some transitions replace a semantically incorrect specification, while others replace an evaluator-unknown formulation with one Verina can certify. Appendix Table A.1 and Section A.4 report both kinds of evidence. Taken together, elicitation is configuration-dependent rather than uniformly beneficial: positive strict estimates occur in the Sonnet 4.6-to-GPT-5.6 and Sonnet 4.6-to-Gemini pipelines, while postcondition degradation offsets potential gains in other configurations. 5 Discussion The results support a pipeline-level rather than formalizer-level interpretation. Clarification can help, but its effect depends on both the elicited handoff and its translation into Lean. Because every cross-model configuration independently samples its dialogue and handoff, those comparisons do not isolate the receiving formalizer or rank formalizers on a shared specification. Compile-conditional estimates are likewise diagnostic because baseline and treatment condition on different compiling subsets, and differences across Verina’s difficulty labels do not establish difficulty or underspecification as a causal moderator. Postconditions are the clearest bottleneck: useful task information can be lost when a richer handoff becomes an incomplete, over-specific, or otherwise incorrect Lean postcondition. The qualitative cases also distinguish semantic repair from evaluator certification: ComputeAvg has a concrete baseline counterexample, whereas the LongestCommonPrefix and RunLengthEncode baselines fail strict scoring only because some Verina checks return UNKNOWN . Interactive-autoformalization evaluations should therefore separate information acquired during elicitation, its translation into a formal artifact, and the evaluator’s ability to certify that artifact. These results concern the controlled pipeline and do not establish performance with human developers. 6 Limitations The study answers the two research questions within a controlled benchmark setting, not a deployed human-facing workflow. Verina’s task distribution and Lean idioms may not represent other verification settings or industrial workflows ( Ye et al., 2025 ) . The reference-grounded simulated developer may also be more precise and consistent than an ordinary developer. Robustness to an imperfect answer source should be evaluated by systematically masking reference fields and injecting omissions, uncertainty, or inconsistent answers, then measuring how performance degrades. Transfer to human intent elicitation additionally requires real-developer studies with interface, trust, and accessibility evaluation ( Trinh et al., 2026 ; Raghavendra et al., 2026 ) . The experiment does not compare EA-selected questions against another question-selection policy using the same simulated developer and question budget. Consequently, it measures the value of the complete EA–simulated-developer interaction, not whether this EA selects better questions than fixed or generic clarification strategies. A question-policy control would hold the answer source and interaction budget fixed while varying only which questions are asked. The question budgets are upper bounds, and the EA often stops before exhausting them. Because the realized number of questions depends on the task-specific state produced during elicitation, comparisons between k = 3 k=3 and k = 10 k=10 do not identify a causal effect of dialogue length. A fixed-turn experiment or a design that randomizes continuation after each exchange would be needed to isolate that effect. The primary experiments use only Sonnet 4.6 as the EA and simulated developer. Moreover, each cross-model arm independently samples its dialogue and refined description, so the arms differ in both handoff and receiving formalizer; the auxiliary all-GPT-5.6 run changes every role. The results therefore compare complete configurations rather than isolating role-specific effects. A clean study would reuse saved handoffs across formalizers and separately evaluate non-Claude EAs and simulated developers under the same protocol. The number of tested models is too small to support provider- or training-lineage claims. Evaluating model-role effects requires more Claude and non-Claude formalizers, non-Claude EAs, reverse cross-model pairings, and shared-handoff interventions that constrain postcondition structure. The evaluation is limited to specification generation and does not test downstream proof or code generation ( Ye et al., 2025 ) . It does not independently score the refined descriptions, and Verina treats UNKNOWN as strict failure; gains may therefore reflect either semantic correction or more certifiable reformulation. The qualitative examples distinguish these mechanisms but do not estimate their prevalence. Uncertainty intervals capture task-level variation, not repeated-generation variance, and the experiments do not establish the most cost-effective allocation of models across roles. The work could reduce specification mismatch, but deploying it without human review could also create false confidence when the answer source or formalizer is wrong; verifier checks mitigate but do not eliminate that risk. 7 Conclusion This paper studied whether an elicitation agent can obtain useful information from a reference-grounded simulated developer before Lean formalization. Reference-grounded clarification has positive verifier-checked point estimates in some complete pipeline configurations, but not uniformly; postconditions are the largest source of degradation. Because dialogues are resampled across configurations, the study does not isolate formalizer effects, and it does not establish performance with imperfect or human developers. Future work should compare question-selection policies, reuse shared handoffs to isolate model roles, vary the EA and answer source, and test human clarification. References Asawa et al.
